title: St Patrick's Day argument: DARPA as Corso's conduit
summary: John Blitch tells of St Patrick's Day argument: DARPA as Corso's conduit, about 2001 (about 1958 onward) at DARPA office, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

plain: John Blitch, a scientist who worked at DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, says that around 2001, on a St Patrick's Day, he argued a case in a DARPA office. He says he made the case that DARPA grew out of the section run by General Trudeau where Philip Corso served, Corso being an Army officer whose book The Day After Roswell says he helped pass on technology from a craft said to have crashed near Roswell, New Mexico, in 1947. In Blitch's telling, DARPA became the channel that broke that technology into parts and handed them out, which would mean crash material quietly shaped modern American inventions.
